{"markdown":"# Issues Memo — Master Services Agreement

**To:** Deal team  
**From:** In-house counsel (Customer side)  
**Re:** Playbook review of Vendor's Master Services Agreement — verified findings

---

## 1. Executive summary

We reviewed the Agreement against the playbook and verified 19 findings. Eleven clauses sit at or above our preferred position and require no redline — notably the mutual liability cap and carve-outs (§ 21), the licence grant package (§ 13), assignment and change of control (§ 24), renewal mechanics (§ 8.2–8.3), Vendor's audit rights (§ 22), the performance warranty suite (§ 19) and insurance (§ 18).

Eight items need attention, and several are serious. Three are critical: the Agreement contains **no indemnification clause at all** (the numbering jumps from § 19 to § 21) even though §§ 9.3, 19.4, 19.5, 21.3, 29.2 and 30.5 all presuppose one; § 14.2 gives Vendor exclusive ownership of every Deliverable we pay for, with only a revocable term-limited licence back; and there is no post-termination transition assistance or Customer Data return mechanic anywhere in a hosted-services deal.

A cluster of Customer-side restrictions is also unacceptable and, tellingly, internally inconsistent: § 12.4 imposes an undefined-scope non-compete and an all-personnel no-hire for the term plus 24 months, § 7.2 imposes a disclose-and-match MFN obligation, and § 2.1 imposes a three-year USD 2,000,000 per year take-or-pay commitment "without reduction or termination rights" — all of which contradict § 12.3, where Vendor acknowledges that Customer has made no exclusivity, non-compete, most-favoured-customer, minimum-volume or no-hire commitment. Separately, § 28.1 selects Singapore law and exclusive Singapore jurisdiction, which conflicts with § 28.2's New York County exclusive venue, and there is no Customer termination-for-convenience right.

## 2. Findings

| # | Severity | Rule | Status | Section | Summary / position |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Critical | INDEMN — Indemnification by Vendor | Missing | § 9.3 (cross-refers to a non-existent § 20.5) | No indemnity exists anywhere; numbering jumps § 19 → § 21. We insert a new § 20 at the preferred level (IP infringement, breach of Applicable Law, Vendor-caused unauthorized access to Customer Data, gross negligence/wilful misconduct) with notice, control of defence and cooperation, plus a narrow Customer indemnity. We did not take the fallback: its 3× fees super-cap is worse than § 21.3, which already treats indemnification as an uncapped Excluded Claim. |
| 2 | Critical | IP — Ownership of Deliverables and Customer Data | Deviation | § 14.2 | Vendor exclusively owns every Deliverable; Customer gets a revocable, non-transferable, term-limited licence. Fails even the fallback (perpetual, irrevocable, worldwide, royalty-free licence to use, modify, sublicense). Cure: reverse to Customer ownership with express assignment. §§ 14.1, 14.3, 14.4, 13.2 already sit at preferred. |
| 3 | Critical | LOL-CAP — Limitation of liability | Compliant | § 21.1 (with §§ 21.2–21.4) | Preferred position met: mutual cap at greater of 12 months' Fees paid or payable and USD 1,000,000; mutual consequential-damages exclusion with restoration/incident costs confirmed as direct; robust uncapped Excluded Claims. No redline. |
| 4 | Critical | TRANSITION — Exit assistance and data return | Missing | § 10.1 | No exit assistance and no Customer Data return/deletion mechanic; § 16.5 defers Customer Data to §§ 11 and 15, which contain no export or deletion timing. Fails the fallback. We insert § 10.3: six months' assistance at then-current rates, return in machine-readable format within 30 days, certified deletion thereafter. |
| 5 | High | NONCOMPETE — Non-compete on Customer | Deviation | § 12.4 | Term plus 24 months, "any product or service that competes with Vendor", any territory. Walk-away on post-term duration and undefined scope; fails every fallback element. Cure: delete the Customer non-compete, restoring consistency with § 12.3. |
| 6 | High | NOSOLICIT — Non-solicitation of employees | Deviation | § 12.4 | One-sided, all-Vendor-employee no-hire for term plus 24 months, "regardless of how the employee applies" (no general-advertising or unsolicited-approach carve-out). Walk-away. Cure: replace with confirmation that Customer takes no such restriction. |
| 7 | High | T4C — Termination for convenience | Deviation | § 2.1 (with §§ 8.1, 9, 10.2) | Three-year term with no Customer convenience right; § 2.1 says "without reduction or termination rights". § 8.2 non-renewal and § 27.3 force majeure are not substitutes, and § 10.2's refund is not expressly pro rata. Cure: new § 9.4 — 30 days' notice, pro-rata refund of all prepaid Fees, no Vendor convenience termination during a committed term. |
| 8 | High | ASSIGN — Assignment and change of control | Compliant | § 24.1 (with §§ 24.2–24.4, 13.3) | Preferred: notice-only Customer assignment to Affiliates/successors, Vendor assignment gated by our consent, competitor bar, and § 24.4 denies Vendor any repricing or termination on our change of control. No redline. |
| 9 | High | EXCLUSIVITY — Exclusivity binding Customer | Compliant | § 12.3 | Preferred: express freedom to develop, acquire, license or use any product and engage any supplier; no sole-supplier or all-requirements clause. §§ 7.2, 2.1 and 12.4 are handled under MFN, MINCOMMIT and NONCOMPETE and not double-flagged. |
| 10 | High | LD — Liquidated damages / penalties | Compliant | § 27.3 (with §§ 9, 10, 7.3, 22.2) | No liquidated damages, penalty or early-termination fee on Customer; § 27.3 permits termination "without penalty" with refund. § 22.2 recovers actual audit costs only. No redline. |
| 11 | High | LICENSE — Licence grant scope | Compliant | § 13.1 (with §§ 13.2, 13.3, 14.3) | Preferred: Affiliates and contractors covered in the grant; perpetual irrevocable licence for paid-up software and Vendor Technology; revocation limited to uncured material breach; transferable on a permitted § 24 assignment. § 14.2 conflict addressed under IP. |
| 12 | Medium | GOVLAW — Governing law and venue | Deviation | § 28.1 | Singapore law and exclusive Singapore jurisdiction — outside the accepted list and walk-away on its face; also contradicts § 28.2 (exclusive New York County venue). Cure: New York law in § 28.1 and delete the Singapore jurisdiction wording, leaving § 28.2 intact. |
| 13 | Medium | MFN — Most-favoured-nation burdening Customer | Deviation | § 7.2 | Open-ended obligation to disclose and match any more favourable offer before engaging another provider — no defined product, time limit or like-for-like carve-outs; fails the fallback and contradicts § 12.3. Cure: replace with an express statement that no disclose-or-match obligation applies. |
| 14 | Medium | MINCOMMIT — Minimum purchase commitments | Deviation | § 2.1 | Three-year USD 2,000,000 per year take-or-pay "without reduction or termination rights"; no 12-month limit, no reduction right, no true-up, no convenience exit. Walk-away, and contradicts § 12.3. Cure: replace with an express no-minimum-commitment statement (§ 7.1 already limits us to Order Form Fees). |
| 15 | Medium | AUDIT — Audit rights against Customer | Compliant | § 22.1 (with §§ 22.2, 22.3) | Preferred: once per 12 months, 30 days' notice, business hours, off-site where practicable, independent auditor under confidentiality, Vendor-borne costs unless >5% underpayment, no direct system access, findings are our Confidential Information. No redline. |
| 16 | Medium | RENEWAL — Auto-renewal and notice window | Compliant | § 8.2 (with § 8.3) | Preferred: 12-month renewals, 30-day Customer opt-out, 60-day Vendor reminder with deadline extension if missed, uplift capped at lesser of CPI and 3%. No redline. |
| 17 | Medium | WARRANTY — Performance warranty and duration | Compliant | § 19.1 (with §§ 19.2–19.5) | At or above preferred: professional/workmanlike and conformance warranties, 90-day Deliverable period plus full-term hosted conformance, law-compliance and no-malicious-code warranties, non-exclusive remedies, and § 19.5 prevents the disclaimer swallowing the warranty. No redline. |
| 18 | Low | INSURANCE — Vendor insurance | Compliant | § 18.1 (with § 18.2) | Preferred limits met in full (CGL 1M/2M, E&O 2M, cyber/privacy 5M, workers' comp, employer's liability), term plus one year, certificates on request. No redline. |

## 3. Walk-away items

The following must be resolved before signature. Each is identified in the verified findings as walk-away territory or as a failure of the fallback on a material term:

1. **No Vendor indemnity (missing § 20).** We have no IP, breach-of-law, data-breach or misconduct indemnity, while six other sections assume one exists. Non-negotiable.
2. **§ 14.2 — Vendor ownership of Deliverables.** Fails even the fallback licence-back. We require Customer ownership with express assignment.
3. **§ 12.4 — non-compete (term + 24 months, undefined scope) and all-personnel no-hire (term + 24 months, no carve-outs).** Both walk-away; both contradict § 12.3.
4. **§ 2.1 — three-year USD 2,000,000 per year take-or-pay without reduction or termination rights.** Walk-away; contradicts § 12.3 and is compounded by the absence of any convenience exit.
5. **§ 28.1 — Singapore law and exclusive Singapore jurisdiction.** Outside the accepted list (New York, Delaware, California, England and Wales) and inconsistent with § 28.2.
6. **§ 7.2 — open-ended disclose-and-match MFN.** Fails the fallback and approaches walk-away; contradicts § 12.3.
7. **No transition assistance or Customer Data return (missing from § 10).** Fails the fallback in a hosted-services deal where our data sits with Vendor.

## 4. Next steps

1. **Issue the redline** covering the eight deviation and missing items: new § 20 (Vendor indemnity with notice/control/cooperation and a narrow Customer indemnity); § 14.2 reversed to Customer ownership with assignment; new § 10.3 (six months' assistance, 30-day machine-readable data return, certified deletion); new § 9.4 (30-day convenience right with pro-rata refund of prepaid Fees, no Vendor convenience termination during a committed term) with § 2.1 conformed; § 12.4 restrictions removed; § 7.2 MFN obligation replaced; § 2.1 replaced with a no-minimum-commitment statement; § 28.1 changed to New York law with the Singapore jurisdiction wording deleted.
2. **Lead with the internal inconsistencies.** §§ 2.1, 7.2 and 12.4 each contradict Vendor's own acknowledgement in § 12.3, and § 28.1 contradicts § 28.2. These are the cheapest wins and should be framed as conforming the document to Vendor's stated positions.
3. **Flag the drafting gap in § 20** to Vendor directly, noting the § 9.3, 19.4, 19.5, 21.3, 29.2 and 30.5 cross-references to obligations the document never creates; we expect Vendor to treat this as an error rather than a negotiation.
4. **Confirm with the business** the commercial appetite on § 2.1 volume and § 12.4 competing-product scope, so we know which fallbacks (if any) we are authorised to accept.
5. **Hold the compliant clauses.** §§ 13, 18, 19, 21, 22, 24, 8.2–8.3, 12.3 and 27.3 sit at or above our preferred position; we should resist any reopening of these as consideration for the changes above.
"}
